title: Kelowna Home Energy Rebates 2026: FortisBC Electricity Customers
desc: Kelowna rebates for 2026: FortisBC pays for insulation, windows, water heaters and thermostats because FortisBC supplies Kelowna's electricity.
lead: Most BC pages start with BC Hydro. Kelowna's electricity comes from FortisBC, so the rebates you can claim are FortisBC's, and the BC Hydro amounts shown on other cities' pages do not apply to your power bill.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Kelowna in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

sections: FortisBC substations serve downtown and south-central Kelowna, and FortisBC is the electric utility for the city. FortisBC's rebates use the same per-R formula as BC Hydro for insulation (attic up to $900, walls and basement up to $1,200 each, other spots up to $1,000), $100 per window or door up to $2,000, up to $1,000 for a heat pump water heater, up to $150 for a connected thermostat on electric central heat, and 50% of an EV charger up to $350. We did not verify a FortisBC heat pump rebate for electric customers, so ask before you book.

The 2021 Census counted 62,210 households. 32% live in homes built before 1981, 43% in detached houses, 65% own. There are 8,205 owner-occupied detached houses from before 1981. Major repairs were reported by 3.9%, the second-lowest share in our set. The older houses are where FortisBC's insulation formula pays the most.

The January average low is -3.2°C and the record low in 2015 to 2024 was -24.0°C. Solar produces about 3.72 peak sun hours a day, the second-best figure in this set, but the rebate in BC Hydro's solar program is for BC Hydro customers, so ask FortisBC and your installer what applies to you.
How to tell which utility applies to your house

Look at the name on your electricity bill, not the street. FortisBC supplies Kelowna, but BC Hydro pages on other cities do not describe your rebates. A quick check avoids a common mistake: applying to the wrong utility and being turned away after the work is done. If you moved into the house recently, the account holder's name must match the application, or the previous owner's account may still be the one on file.

FortisBC also asks you to read each rebate's eligibility tab before you buy. The deadlines and per-item rules sit there, not on the summary page.

We could not confirm a FortisBC heat pump rebate for electric customers, and we did not verify whether BC Hydro's solar and battery programs extend to FortisBC accounts. Both are on our list to re-read. Until we do, treat any quote that includes a rebate for either as unconfirmed and ask the installer for the program page.
If you heat with gas or have a lower income

CleanBC pays $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000 for income-qualified households replacing gas, oil or propane with a central or three-head heat pump. FortisBC also lists free evaluations and upgrades for income-qualified customers.

claim_steps: Check that FortisBC is your electric supplier.
Pick the upgrade: insulation, windows or water heater.
Take quotes that name the R-value or U-factor.
Ask FortisBC about a second-upgrade bonus.
Apply within the FortisBC deadline on its listing.
faq: Not to a FortisBC electric account. Use FortisBC's listing.
$300 for a second upgrade, or $750 to $2,000 if the EnerGuide rating improves enough.
Does Kelowna get colder than Vancouver?
Yes. The record low in 2015 to 2024 was -24.0 degrees against -14.1 in Vancouver.
